A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepASA research and are readable throughout, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched despite revised diagrams, table relocation, the addition of Appendix G, and removal of the NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, dereverberation results, and case analyses in the main text and Appendices B–F.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds pretraining controls, repeated-CoI experiments, measured-room-response evaluation, and source-count stress tests.

M1.justification: Section 2.5 revises the reported CoI training procedure: v1 freezes all of Net 1 when training Net 2, whereas v3 freezes only through Net 1's third DeFT-Mamba block. The core architecture remains intact; expanded descriptions of SED outputs, PIT, and window training largely provide clarification rather than establish new components.

E1.justification: The three named benchmarks and office demonstration remain. Appendices F–G add evaluation using mixtures generated with measured room impulse responses, including unseen responses, and scenes containing six or seven foreground sources beyond the five-source capacity. These substantially extend environmental and source-overlap test coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding MC-FUSS, STARSS23, and ASA2 comparisons retain their external comparison methods. Added rows examine different training conditions for the existing DeFT-Mamba comparator and ablated DeepASA configurations; they do not introduce another comparator algorithm.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes reported STARSS23 augmentation from 20 to 80 hours. Table 3 adds scratch-versus-ASA2-pretrained controls, while new appendix experiments vary CoI depth and fine-tune on measured-response mixtures before testing unseen responses. The CoI freezing rule also changes. These are reported protocol differences; retained scores do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations and case studies, v3 tests dependence on pretraining and ATST, whether repeating CoI helps, transfer to measured room responses, and failure beyond the source-capacity limit (Tables 3 and 8–11). These add substantial controls and robustness analyses addressing previously untested questions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-trial means and standard deviations in Section 4.2 and the corresponding result tables. Removing v1's checklist removes its explicit statement that those runs used different random seeds and its unelaborated significance-testing claim. No change in actual run count or uncertainty-estimation procedure is established.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds DeepASA-without-ATST results of 17.5 dB from scratch and 18.4 dB after pretraining, while retaining the 18.5 dB headline result. Reported DeepASA complexity changes from 3.8 M parameters/84.0 G MAC/s to 2.9 M/77.3 G. New appendix results include SELD scores of 0.216 for a second CoI stage, 0.254 with measured room responses, and 0.418/0.521 for six/seven sources. These are newly evaluated conditions, not same-setting performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: The signal-mixture equation and underlying mathematical formulation are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs, and v3's tensor dimensions and notation clarifications do not introduce substantive new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the unified multi-task ASA contribution, object-oriented processing, CoI refinement, and state-of-the-art performance claims. Changing 'One-for-All' to 'Multi-Purpose' does not materially change the stated task scope or contributions.

C2.justification: v1 mainly identifies ATST's parameter cost as a limitation. v3 adds anticipated reverberation/noise limits and eavesdropping misuse, interprets repeated-CoI degradation as excessive emphasis on temporal coherence, attributes measured-response degradation to representation mismatch, and explains over-capacity failures through merged sources. These materially expand applicability boundaries and failure explanations.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release in its checklist; v3's abstract reports code availability alongside the demo. v3 also documents the window freeze/unfreeze schedule, PIT for foreground decoders but not noise, TCM's temporal sequence dimension, and simulated reverberation/SNR ranges. These improve implementation disclosure without establishing that each detail represents a newly adopted procedure.

R1.justification: v3 adds Yu et al.'s 2017 permutation-invariant-training paper as reference 44. All 58 earlier references remain, and the substantive USS, TSE, and SELD positioning is largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and timestamp/activation terminology, expands selected method explanations, adds acknowledgements and Appendix G, and removes the NeurIPS checklist. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain, so this is targeted editing rather than extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Figures 4(b) and 5 are substantially redrawn to clarify shared object decoders and simplify CoI's depiction. Table 3 gains training-regime groups, three new tables display CoI depth, room-response transfer, and source-count results, and the expanded ASA2 comparison moves from Table 8 to Table 9. Most other figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Pretraining/ATST controls strengthen performance attribution, while the new negative results clarify limits of repeated refinement and generalization. Clearer implementation descriptions and limitations also help. The gains are tempered by sparse protocols for the new tests, unchanged STARSS23 scores despite revised augmentation, and Table 11's seven-source 'Bottom 2' label conflicting with its three-source explanation. Overall, v3 provides a useful but qualified improvement to an already extensively evaluated paper.
